audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Deuteronomy / Devarim Og, Transjordan allocation, Joshua charge, and Moses plea retelling, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Og warfare, total-destruction language, giant-bed tradition, Transjordan allocation, armed-vanguard obligation, Joshua encouragement, and Moses' denied entry.

verses.restored: We turned and went up way of Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us, he and all his people, for battle at Edrei.

familiar.text: Then we turned, and went up the way to Bashan: and Og the king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.

modern.text: Then we turned and went up the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan and his whole army came out to meet us in battle at Edrei.

original.text: וַנֵּ֣פֶן וַנַּ֔עַל דֶּ֖רֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֑ן וַיֵּצֵ֣א עוֹג֩ מֶֽלֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֨ן לִקְרָאתֵ֜נוּ ה֧וּא וְכָל עַמּ֛וֹ לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אֶדְרֶֽעִי

verses.restored: YHWH said to me, Do not fear him, for into your hand I have given him and all his people and his land; you shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of Amorite dwelling in Heshbon.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto me, Fear him not: for I will deliver him, and all his people, and his land, into thy hand; and thou shalt do unto him as thou didst unto Sihon king of the Amorites, which dwelt at Heshbon.

modern.text: But the LORD said to me, “Do not fear him, for I have delivered him into your hand, along with all his people and his land. Do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֵלַי֙ אַל תִּירָ֣א אֹת֔וֹ כִּ֣י בְיָדְךָ֞ נָתַ֧תִּי אֹת֛וֹ וְאֶת כָּל עַמּ֖וֹ וְאֶת אַרְצ֑וֹ וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֗יתָ לְסִיחֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּחֶשְׁבּֽוֹן

verses.restored: YHWH our Divine also gave into our hand Og king of Bashan and all his people, and we struck him until no survivor remained to him.

familiar.text: So the LORD our God delivered into our hands Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people: and we smote him until none was left to him remaining.

modern.text: So the LORD our God also delivered Og king of Bashan and his whole army into our hands. We struck them down until no survivor was left.

original.text: וַיִּתֵּן֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֜ינוּ בְּיָדֵ֗נוּ גַּ֛ם אֶת ע֥וֹג מֶֽלֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֖ן וְאֶת כָּל עַמּ֑וֹ וַנַּכֵּ֕הוּ עַד בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִֽיר ל֖וֹ שָׂרִֽיד

verses.restored: We captured all his cities at that time; there was not a town we did not take from them, sixty cities, all region of Argob, kingdom of Og in Bashan.

familiar.text: And we took all his cities at that time, there was not a city which we took not from them, threescore cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

modern.text: At that time we captured all sixty of his cities. There was not a single city we failed to take—the entire region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

original.text: וַנִּלְכֹּ֤ד אֶת כָּל עָרָיו֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔וא לֹ֤א הָֽיְתָה֙ קִרְיָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא לָקַ֖חְנוּ מֵֽאִתָּ֑ם שִׁשִּׁ֥ים עִיר֙ כָּל חֶ֣בֶל אַרְגֹּ֔ב מַמְלֶ֥כֶת ע֖וֹג בַּבָּשָֽׁן

verses.restored: All these were fortified cities with high walls, gates, and bars, besides very many unwalled villages.

familiar.text: All these cities were fenced with high walls, gates, and bars; beside unwalled towns a great many.

modern.text: All these cities were fortified with high walls and gates and bars, and there were many more unwalled villages.

original.text: כָּל אֵ֜לֶּה עָרִ֧ים בְּצֻר֛וֹת חוֹמָ֥ה גְבֹהָ֖ה דְּלָתַ֣יִם וּבְרִ֑יחַ לְבַ֛ד מֵעָרֵ֥י הַפְּרָזִ֖י הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: We devoted them to destruction as we did to Sihon king of Heshbon, devoting every city—men, women, and little ones.

familiar.text: And we utterly destroyed them, as we did unto Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying the men, women, and children, of every city.

modern.text: We devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying the men, women, and children of every city.

original.text: וַנַּחֲרֵ֣ם אוֹתָ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔ינוּ לְסִיחֹ֖ן מֶ֣לֶךְ חֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן הַחֲרֵם֙ כָּל עִ֣יר מְתִ֔ם הַנָּשִׁ֖ים וְהַטָּֽף

verses.restored: But all livestock and spoil of cities we plundered for ourselves.

familiar.text: But all the cattle, and the spoil of the cities, we took for a prey to ourselves.

modern.text: But all the livestock and plunder of the cities we carried off for ourselves.

original.text: וְכָל הַבְּהֵמָ֛ה וּשְׁלַ֥ל הֶעָרִ֖ים בַּזּ֥וֹנוּ לָֽנוּ

verses.restored: At that time we took land from hand of two kings of Amorite across Jordan, from wadi Arnon to Mount Hermon.

familiar.text: And we took at that time out of the hand of the two kings of the Amorites the land that was on this side Jordan, from the river of Arnon unto mount Hermon;

modern.text: At that time we took from the two kings of the Amorites the land across the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley as far as Mount Hermon—

original.text: וַנִּקַּ֞ח בָּעֵ֤ת הַהִוא֙ אֶת הָאָ֔רֶץ מִיַּ֗ד שְׁנֵי֙ מַלְכֵ֣י הָאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן מִנַּ֥חַל אַרְנֹ֖ן עַד הַ֥ר חֶרְמֽוֹן

verses.restored: Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and Amorites call it Senir.

familiar.text: (Which Hermon the Sidonians call Sirion; and the Amorites call it Shenir;)

modern.text: which the Sidonians call Sirion but the Amorites call Senir—

original.text: צִידֹנִ֛ים יִקְרְא֥וּ לְחֶרְמ֖וֹן שִׂרְיֹ֑ן וְהָ֣אֱמֹרִ֔י יִקְרְאוּ ל֖וֹ שְׂנִֽיר

verses.restored: All cities of plateau, all Gilead, and all Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of kingdom of Og in Bashan.

familiar.text: All the cities of the plain, and all Gilead, and all Bashan, unto Salchah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

modern.text: all the cities of the plateau, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as the cities of Salecah and Edrei in the kingdom of Og.

original.text: כֹּ֣ל עָרֵ֣י הַמִּישֹׁ֗ר וְכָל הַגִּלְעָד֙ וְכָל הַבָּשָׁ֔ן עַד סַלְכָ֖ה וְאֶדְרֶ֑עִי עָרֵ֛י מַמְלֶ֥כֶת ע֖וֹג בַּבָּשָֽׁן

verses.restored: For only Og king of Bashan remained from remnant of Rephaim. Look, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron; is it not in Rabbah of sons of Ammon? Nine cubits its length and four cubits its width, by cubit of man.

familiar.text: For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants; behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron; is it not in Rabbath of the children of Ammon? nine cubits was the length thereof, and four cubits the breadth of it, after the cubit of a man.

modern.text: (For only Og king of Bashan had remained of the remnant of the Rephaim. His bed of iron, nine cubits long and four cubits wide, is still in Rabbah of the Ammonites.) Land Division East of the Jordan (Numbers 32:1–42; Joshua 13:8–14)

original.text: כִּ֣י רַק ע֞וֹג מֶ֣לֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֗ן נִשְׁאַר֮ מִיֶּ֣תֶר הָרְפָאִים֒ הִנֵּ֤ה עַרְשׂוֹ֙ עֶ֣רֶשׂ בַּרְזֶ֔ל הֲלֹ֣ה הִ֔וא בְּרַבַּ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן תֵּ֧שַׁע אַמּ֣וֹת אָרְכָּ֗הּ וְאַרְבַּ֥ע אַמּ֛וֹת רָחְבָּ֖הּ בְּאַמַּת אִֽישׁ

verses.restored: This land we possessed at that time: from Aroer beside wadi Arnon and half hill country of Gilead and its cities I gave to Reubenites and Gadites.

familiar.text: And this land, which we possessed at that time, from Aroer, which is by the river Arnon, and half mount Gilead, and the cities thereof, gave I unto the Reubenites and to the Gadites.

modern.text: So at that time we took possession of this land. To the Reubenites and Gadites I gave the land beyond Aroer along the Arnon Valley, and half the hill country of Gilead, along with its cities.

original.text: וְאֶת הָאָ֧רֶץ הַזֹּ֛את יָרַ֖שְׁנוּ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑וא מֵעֲרֹעֵ֞ר אֲשֶׁר עַל נַ֣חַל אַרְנֹ֗ן וַחֲצִ֤י הַֽר הַגִּלְעָד֙ וְעָרָ֔יו נָתַ֕תִּי לָרֻֽאוּבֵנִ֖י וְלַגָּדִֽי

verses.restored: The rest of Gilead and all Bashan, kingdom of Og, I gave to half tribe of Manasseh; all region of Argob, all that Bashan, was called land of Rephaim.

familiar.text: And the rest of Gilead, and all Bashan, being the kingdom of Og, gave I unto the half tribe of Manasseh; all the region of Argob, with all Bashan, which was called the land of giants.

modern.text: To the half-tribe of Manasseh I gave the rest of Gilead and all of Bashan, the kingdom of Og. (The entire region of Argob, the whole territory of Bashan, used to be called the land of the Rephaim.)

original.text: וְיֶ֨תֶר הַגִּלְעָ֤ד וְכָל הַבָּשָׁן֙ מַמְלֶ֣כֶת ע֔וֹג נָתַ֕תִּי לַחֲצִ֖י שֵׁ֣בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּׁ֑ה כֹּ֣ל חֶ֤בֶל הָֽאַרְגֹּב֙ לְכָל הַבָּשָׁ֔ן הַה֥וּא יִקָּרֵ֖א אֶ֥רֶץ רְפָאִֽים

verses.restored: Jair son of Manasseh took all region of Argob as far as border of Geshurites and Maacathites and called them by his name, Bashan-havvoth-jair, until this day.

familiar.text: Jair the son of Manasseh took all the country of Argob unto the coasts of Geshuri and Maachathi; and called them after his own name, Bashanhavothjair, unto this day.

modern.text: Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites. He renamed Bashan after himself, Havvoth-jair, by which it is called to this day.

original.text: יָאִ֣יר בֶּן מְנַשֶּׁ֗ה לָקַח֙ אֶת כָּל חֶ֣בֶל אַרְגֹּ֔ב עַד גְּב֥וּל הַגְּשׁוּרִ֖י וְהַמַּֽעֲכָתִ֑י וַיִּקְרָא֩ אֹתָ֨ם עַל שְׁמ֤וֹ אֶת הַבָּשָׁן֙ חַוֺּ֣ת יָאִ֔יר עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: To Machir I gave Gilead.

familiar.text: And I gave Gilead unto Machir.

modern.text: To Machir I gave Gilead,

original.text: וּלְמָכִ֖יר נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת הַגִּלְעָֽד

verses.restored: To Reubenites and Gadites I gave from Gilead as far as wadi Arnon, middle of wadi as border, as far as wadi Jabbok, border of sons of Ammon;

familiar.text: And unto the Reubenites and unto the Gadites I gave from Gilead even unto the river Arnon half the valley, and the border even unto the river Jabbok, which is the border of the children of Ammon;

modern.text: and to the Reubenites and Gadites I gave the territory from Gilead to the Arnon Valley (the middle of the valley was the border) and up to the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites.

original.text: וְלָרֻאוּבֵנִ֨י וְלַגָּדִ֜י נָתַ֤תִּי מִן הַגִּלְעָד֙ וְעַד נַ֣חַל אַרְנֹ֔ן תּ֥וֹךְ הַנַּ֖חַל וּגְבֻ֑ל וְעַד֙ יַבֹּ֣ק הַנַּ֔חַל גְּב֖וּל בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן

verses.restored: and Arabah, with Jordan as border, from Chinnereth as far as sea of Arabah, Salt Sea, below slopes of Pisgah eastward.

familiar.text: The plain also, and Jordan, and the coast thereof, from Chinnereth even unto the sea of the plain, even the salt sea, under Ashdothpisgah eastward.

modern.text: The Jordan River in the Arabah bordered it from Chinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah (the Salt Sea ) with the slopes of Pisgah to the east.

original.text: וְהָֽעֲרָבָ֖ה וְהַיַּרְדֵּ֣ן וּגְבֻ֑ל מִכִּנֶּ֗רֶת וְעַ֨ד יָ֤ם הָֽעֲרָבָה֙ יָ֣ם הַמֶּ֔לַח תַּ֛חַת אַשְׁדֹּ֥ת הַפִּסְגָּ֖ה מִזְרָֽחָה

verses.restored: I commanded you at that time, saying, YHWH your Divine has given you this land to possess it. All men of strength shall cross over armed before your brothers, children of Israel.

familiar.text: And I commanded you at that time, saying, The LORD your God hath given you this land to possess it: ye shall pass over armed before your brethren the children of Israel, all that are meet for the war.

modern.text: At that time I commanded you: “The LORD your God has given you this land to possess. All your men of valor are to cross over, armed for battle, ahead of your brothers, the Israelites.

original.text: וָאֲצַ֣ו אֶתְכֶ֔ם בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖וא לֵאמֹ֑ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֗ם נָתַ֨ן לָכֶ֜ם אֶת הָאָ֤רֶץ הַזֹּאת֙ לְרִשְׁתָּ֔הּ חֲלוּצִ֣ים תַּֽעַבְר֗וּ לִפְנֵ֛י אֲחֵיכֶ֥ם בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כָּל בְּנֵי חָֽיִל

verses.restored: Only your wives, your little ones, and your livestock—I know you have much livestock—shall dwell in cities I gave you,

familiar.text: But your wives, and your little ones, and your cattle, (for I know that ye have much cattle,) shall abide in your cities which I have given you;

modern.text: But your wives, your children, and your livestock—I know that you have much livestock—may remain in the cities I have given you,

original.text: רַ֠ק נְשֵׁיכֶ֣ם וְטַפְּכֶם֮ וּמִקְנֵכֶם֒ יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּֽי מִקְנֶ֥ה רַ֖ב לָכֶ֑ם יֵֽשְׁבוּ֙ בְּעָ֣רֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לָכֶֽם

verses.restored: until YHWH gives rest to your brothers as to you, and they also possess land YHWH your Divine gives them across Jordan; then you shall return each man to his possession that I gave you.

familiar.text: Until the LORD have given rest unto your brethren, as well as unto you, and until they also possess the land which the LORD your God hath given them beyond Jordan: and then shall ye return every man unto his possession, which I have given you.

modern.text: until the LORD gives rest to your brothers as He has to you, and they too have taken possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving them across the Jordan. Then each of you may return to the possession I have given you.”

original.text: עַ֠ד אֲשֶׁר יָנִ֨יחַ יְהוָ֥ה לַֽאֲחֵיכֶם֮ כָּכֶם֒ וְיָרְשׁ֣וּ גַם הֵ֔ם אֶת הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֛ם נֹתֵ֥ן לָהֶ֖ם בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וְשַׁבְתֶּ֗ם אִ֚ישׁ לִֽירֻשָּׁת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לָכֶֽם

verses.restored: I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, Your eyes have seen all YHWH your Divine did to these two kings; so YHWH will do to all kingdoms where you are crossing.

familiar.text: And I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, Thine eyes have seen all that the LORD your God hath done unto these two kings: so shall the LORD do unto all the kingdoms whither thou passest.

modern.text: And at that time I commanded Joshua: “Your own eyes have seen all that the LORD your God has done to these two kings. The LORD will do the same to all the kingdoms you are about to enter.

original.text: וְאֶת יְהוֹשׁ֣וּעַ צִוֵּ֔יתִי בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖וא לֵאמֹ֑ר עֵינֶ֣יךָ הָרֹאֹ֗ת אֵת֩ כָּל אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם֙ לִשְׁנֵי֙ הַמְּלָכִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה כֵּֽן יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְכָל הַמַּמְלָכ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֖ה עֹבֵ֥ר שָֽׁמָּה

verses.restored: You shall not fear them, for YHWH your Divine, he is the one fighting for you.

familiar.text: Ye shall not fear them: for the LORD your God he shall fight for you.

modern.text: Do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God Himself will fight for you.” Moses Forbidden to Cross the Jordan (Numbers 27:12–17)

original.text: לֹ֖א תְִּירָא֑וּם כִּ֚י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם ה֖וּא הַנִּלְחָ֥ם לָכֶֽם

verses.restored: I pleaded with YHWH at that time, saying,

familiar.text: And I besought the LORD at that time, saying,

modern.text: At that time I also pleaded with the LORD:

original.text: וָאֶתְחַנַּ֖ן אֶל יְהוָ֑ה בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖וא לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: Lord YHWH, you have begun to show your servant your greatness and your strong hand, for what divine in heavens or earth can do according to your works and according to your mighty deeds?

familiar.text: O Lord GOD, thou hast begun to shew thy servant thy greatness, and thy mighty hand: for what God is there in heaven or in earth, that can do according to thy works, and according to thy might?

modern.text: “O Lord GOD, You have begun to show Your greatness and power to Your servant. For what god in heaven or on earth can perform such works and mighty acts as Yours?

original.text: אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אַתָּ֤ה הַֽחִלּ֨וֹתָ֙ לְהַרְא֣וֹת אֶֽת עַבְדְּךָ֔ אֶ֨ת גָּדְלְךָ֔ וְאֶת יָדְךָ֖ הַחֲזָקָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר מִי אֵל֙ בַּשָּׁמַ֣יִם וּבָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה כְמַעֲשֶׂ֖יךָ וְכִגְבוּרֹתֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Please let me cross and see good land across Jordan, this good hill country and Lebanon.

familiar.text: I pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land that is beyond Jordan, that goodly mountain, and Lebanon.

modern.text: Please let me cross over and see the good land beyond the Jordan—that pleasant hill country as well as Lebanon!”

original.text: אֶעְבְּרָה נָּ֗א וְאֶרְאֶה֙ אֶת הָאָ֣רֶץ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן הָהָ֥ר הַטּ֛וֹב הַזֶּ֖ה וְהַלְּבָנֽוֹן

verses.restored: But YHWH was furious with me because of you and would not listen to me. YHWH said to me, Enough for you; do not speak to me again about this matter.

familiar.text: But the LORD was wroth with me for your sakes, and would not hear me: and the LORD said unto me, Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter.

modern.text: But the LORD was angry with me on account of you, and He would not listen to me. “That is enough,” the LORD said to me. “Do not speak to Me again about this matter.

original.text: וַיִּתְעַבֵּ֨ר יְהוָ֥ה בִּי֙ לְמַ֣עַנְכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖ע אֵלָ֑י וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֵלַי֙ רַב לָ֔ךְ אַל תּ֗וֹסֶף דַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֛י ע֖וֹד בַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Go up to top of Pisgah and lift your eyes westward, northward, southward, and eastward, and see with your eyes, for you shall not cross this Jordan.

familiar.text: Get thee up into the top of Pisgah, and lift up thine eyes westward, and northward, and southward, and eastward, and behold it with thine eyes: for thou shalt not go over this Jordan.

modern.text: Go to the top of Pisgah and look to the west and north and south and east. See the land with your own eyes, for you will not cross this Jordan.

original.text: עֲלֵ֣ה רֹ֣אשׁ הַפִּסְגָּ֗ה וְשָׂ֥א עֵינֶ֛יךָ יָ֧מָּה וְצָפֹ֛נָה וְתֵימָ֥נָה וּמִזְרָ֖חָה וּרְאֵ֣ה בְעֵינֶ֑יךָ כִּי לֹ֥א תַעֲבֹ֖ר אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּ֥ן הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Command Joshua and strengthen him and make him courageous, for he shall cross before this people and he shall cause them to inherit land you see.

familiar.text: But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him: for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land which thou shalt see.

modern.text: But commission Joshua, encourage him, and strengthen him, for he will cross over ahead of the people and enable them to inherit the land that you will see.”

original.text: וְצַ֥ו אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ וְחַזְּקֵ֣הוּ וְאַמְּצֵ֑הוּ כִּי ה֣וּא יַעֲבֹ֗ר לִפְנֵי֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְהוּא֙ יַנְחִ֣יל אוֹתָ֔ם אֶת הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּרְאֶֽה

verses.restored: So we dwelt in valley opposite Beth-peor.

familiar.text: So we abode in the valley over against Bethpeor.

modern.text: So we stayed in the valley opposite Beth-peor.

original.text: וַנֵּ֣שֶׁב בַּגָּ֔יְא מ֖וּל בֵּ֥ית פְּעֽוֹר

translation_notes: Og's giant-bed tradition belongs to ancient Rephaim lore and should not be sensationalized as modern archaeology.
Verse 6 again names men, women, and children in total-destruction warfare. It must remain visible and categorically non-normative for modern ethics.
Transjordan land is allocated to Reuben, Gad, and half Manasseh, with a reciprocal obligation to assist the other tribes.
Women and children remain behind while men cross armed; their vulnerability and labor are not centered in the speech.
Moses' denied entry demonstrates that foundational leadership does not cancel accountability or guarantee possession of the outcome.
Joshua is strengthened publicly for succession rather than inheriting office through family lineage.
safety_note: Never use Deuteronomy 3 to justify genocide, militarized expansion, giant mythology as racial propaganda, or modern territorial seizure. Its constructive strands are reciprocal obligation, accountable succession, and a leader accepting that the work continues without him.
